result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Answer A frames almost every question as a situation on the floor, and its key explains why each tempting wrong option fails, which is what makes a quiz teach. Answer B covers every topic in the session, including fork height and mast tilt, but most of its questions ask new hires to recite a rule or number. Some of B's wrong options are filler, and its key mostly just restates the rule. A also adds a few small details not in the list: report an overweight load, and 'stop' near pedestrians. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B frames every question as a situation on the floor and has plausible wrong options. Its answer key explains why each wrong option fails. It loses a little for adding small extras, such as reporting an overweight load to a supervisor and stopping fully for a pedestrian, and for having no dedicated question on fork height or mast tilt. A covers every topic and stays accurate, but most of its questions ask new hires to recite a rule or number, and its answer key only restates the rule without addressing the tempting wrong answers.
